faq.a: Capacity is how much a container can hold when it is full. We measure it in millilitres and litres.

faq.q: How many millilitres are in a litre?
faq.a: There are 1,000 millilitres in 1 litre. Four cups of 250 millilitres make 1 litre.

faq.q: How much does a cup hold?
faq.a: A measuring cup usually holds about 250 millilitres, which is a quarter of a litre. Cups at home can be a bit bigger or smaller.
asks: How many millilitres in a cup?

faq.q: Is capacity the same as volume?
faq.a: Not quite. Capacity is how much a container can hold. Volume is how much space something takes up, like the juice actually inside. A half-full 1 litre bottle holds only 500 millilitres.
asks: What is the difference between capacity and volume?

faq.q: How do I read a measuring jug?
faq.a: Put the jug on a flat table, bend down so your eyes are level with the liquid, and read the line it reaches. First check what each small line stands for, like 50 or 100 millilitres.
asks: How do I use a measuring jug?
